attachment.cliPrefix: You are a Claude agent, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK.

content.text: I'll start by reading the rules, inputs, templates and the analyze command in parallel.

content.content:
1	# Create mode (`/sc:issue --create "<description>"`)
2	
3	Loaded at the start of create mode. `<R>` is the origin repo (`owner/repo`), `<skill base>` the directory that holds this skill's `SKILL.md`. Files are written to `<D>` = `.dev/issues/draft-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>-<slug>/` until the issue exists, then the directory is renamed to `.dev/issues/<N>/` (default D10). `<slug>` is built from the first words of the description: lower-case it, replace every run of characters other than `a-z` and `0-9` with one `-`, drop any leading or trailing `-`, cut it to at most 40 characters (dropping a trailing `-` left by the cut), and use `untitled` when nothing is left. The slug therefore holds only `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`: never `/`, `.`, `\`, a space or `..`, so `<D>` always stays directly under `.dev/issues/`.
4	
5	Spawn workers with `subagent_type: issue-worker-t<N>` and never pass the `model` parameter.
6	
7	Workers are `~/.claude/agents/issue-worker-t3.md`, `~/.claude/agents/issue-worker-t2.md` and `~/.claude/agents/issue-worker-t1.md` (Claude Code reads the project `.claude/agents/` copy first when one exists). Load `refs/tiers.md` before the first spawn. A worker that needs a codebase pass runs `/sc:analyze` by following `~/.claude/commands/sc/analyze.md` (project `.claude/commands/sc/analyze.md` in a checkout). Every file under `<D>` starts as a copy of its template under `templates/`.
8	
9	Every GitHub CLI call on issues, pull requests or labels passes `--repo <R>`; every `gh api` path is `user` or starts with `repos/<R>/`, never a brace placeholder, with one exception: the T3 lookup worker's read-only GET of `orgs/<owner of R>/issue-fields` (`<owner>` is the part of `<R>` before the slash). No other `orgs/` path is allowed, and the orchestrator and the T1 and T2 workers keep the old rule. Only the orchestrator writes to GitHub: besides `gh issue create --repo <R>` and `gh issue comment <N> --repo <R>`, its only GitHub field write is the POST of `refs/labels.md` (`gh api -X POST repos/<R>/issues/<N>/issue-field-values`). Create mode makes no ClickUp call and no self-assignment (B6).
10	
11	## Wave 0: prerequisites (orchestrator)
12	
13	1. `uv run --no-project python "<skill base>/scripts/origin_repo.py"` prints `<R>` from the `origin` remote; a non-zero exit is STOP `E-NO-ORIGIN`.
14	2. `gh auth status` must succeed; else STOP `E-GH-AUTH`.
15	3. Check that `<slug>` matches `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`; if it does not, rebuild it by the rule above before going on. Create `<D>`.
16	4. Write the description to `<D>/description.md` from `templates/description.md`. An `@path` description is read from that file.
17	
18	## Wave 1: lookup (issue-worker-t3, B13)
19	
20	Spawn `issue-worker-t3` with the job "create lookup", `<R>`, the description's keywords and `<D>`. The worker lists the repo's labels (`gh label list --repo <R> --limit 200 --json name`), reads the issue types of the repo (`gh api repos/<R>/issue-types`) and the Complexity field of the organization (`gh api orgs/<owner of R>/issue-fields`, the one allowed `orgs/` path; it records the id, the data type and the option names of the field named `Complexity`), searches for possible duplicates (`gh issue list --repo <R> --state all --search "<keywords>" --json number,title,state,url --limit 10`) and writes `<D>/scout.md` from `templates/scout-report.md` (create section: `### Repo labels`, `### Repo issue types`, `### Complexity field`, `### Possible duplicates`). A lookup that fails is recorded as `lookup failed: <reason>` and never stops the run. Possible duplicates do not stop the run; they go into the body's related-issues section (default D11).
21	
22	Worker returns no file or an empty one: retry once, then STOP `E-WORKER-NO-OUTPUT` naming the path.
23	
24	## Wave 2: settle the flags
25	
26	"All flags given" means both `--mode` and `--type` were passed. When only one was passed, keep it and choose the missing one as in the "a flag missing" column (default D12).
27	
28	| Depth | All flags given | A flag missing |
29	|---|---|---|
30	| quick | Take the user's flags at face value; the orchestrator writes `<D>/flags.md` | `issue-worker-t2` reads `description.md` and `scout.md` and chooses |
31	| standard | `issue-worker-t2` runs a quick validation of the user's flags; differences become a pushback comment posted after the issue (Wave 5) | `issue-worker-t1` chooses |
32	| deep | Two variants debated: the orchestrator writes `<D>/flags-user.md` (the user's flags) and `issue-worker-t1` writes `<D>/flags-t1.md` (an independent choice), then `Skill sc:adversarial-protocol` with `--compare <D>/flags-user.md,<D>/flags-t1.md --depth quick`; differences become the pushback comment (default D13) | `issue-worker-t1` runs `/sc:analyze` on the code the description touches, then chooses |
33	
34	Every `issue-worker-t1` spawn in this mode (the Wave 2 flag choices and the Wave 4 deep body) follows the T1 -> T2 fallback of `refs/tiers.md`: when `claude-gw-tier1b` is not served to this user, retry the same job once with `issue-worker-t2`, same inputs and output paths. The retry's spawn prompt tells the T2 worker to put `Handled by issue-worker-t2 (tier 2): tier1b is not available to this user.` in the first lines of `flags.md` (or `flags-t1.md`) for a flag job and of `draft-notes.md` for a body job. Only a T2 fallback that is not served is STOP `E-TIER-UNAVAILABLE`; there is no alias fallback.
35	
36	Complexity follows depth, as the issue body pairs them (default D17): `quick` = Simple, `standard` = Medium, `deep` = Complex; the value is the option name of the Complexity field.
37	
38	Every choice is written to `<D>/flags.md` from `templates/flags-decision.md` (mode, type, issue type, complexity, reasons); `flags-user.md` and `flags-t1.md` use the same template. The `Issue type` row is derived by the orchestrator from the mode and the area by the rule of `refs/labels.md` (a bug is Bug, a feature in the area `tests` is Test, any other feature is Feature), after any worker returns. The issue is filed with the user's flags when the user gave them (the pushback comment explains any disagreement; the issue is not silently reclassified), else with the worker's choice.
39	
40	## Wave 3: pick the template
41	
42	Mode selects feature or bug; depth selects simple or complex:
43	
44	| Mode | `quick` or `standard` | `deep` |
45	|---|---|---|
46	| feature | `templates/issue-feature-simple.md` | `templates/issue-feature-complex.md` |
47	| bug | `templates/issue-bug-simple.md` | `templates/issue-bug-complex.md` |
48	
49	## Wave 4: draft the body
50	
51	| Depth | Worker | Codebase pass |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| quick | `issue-worker-t3` | `/sc:analyze --depth quick` on the touched area |
54	| standard | `issue-worker-t2` | `/sc:analyze` (no `--depth`) |
55	| deep | `issue-worker-t1` | `/sc:analyze --depth deep` |
56	
57	At deep depth the `issue-worker-t1` spawn falls back to `issue-worker-t2` as described in Wave 2. The worker fills the chosen template into `<D>/issue-body.md`, keeping every heading and writing "Not known yet" where the description and the codebase pass give nothing (no invented facts), except in the three required plan sections defined in the next subsection. It lists, in `<D>/draft-notes.md` (from `templates/draft-notes.md`), under New material every addition beyond the description (assumptions included), which is kept without any question, and under Contradictions only a supported contradiction of the user's own words. A contradiction is one of exactly four categories: reversed choice (the draft reverses a choice the user stated), dropped requirement (the draft omits a requirement the user stated), changed flag (the drafted issue would not honor `--mode`, `--type` or `--depth` as given) and user-stated fact contradicted by verified code (the worker read the code and the user's stated fact is false). Each contradiction line carries its category, the user's own words in quotes (or the flag as passed) and the conflicting evidence (draft text, or a `path:line` the worker read); a line missing any of the three is recorded as New material instead. An addition that is the only evidence of a contradiction is listed under Contradictions.
58	
59	Secrets rule: the drafting worker never copies anything that looks like a secret (a key, token, password, credential, or a connection string with a password) or any text from `~/.env`, environment variables or credential files into the issue body or the notes. If the draft would contain such material, the worker leaves the value out and lists that under Contradictions (naming the place, never the value), so the contradiction question is asked.
60	
61	### Required plan sections (Priority, Fix approach, Test plan)
62	
63	The three sections `## Priority`, `## Fix approach` and `## Test plan` are the last three headings of every issue-body template, in that order, so an issue arrives with its plan already written and whoever picks it up only executes.
64	
65	At every depth (quick, standard and deep) the worker fills `## Priority`, `## Fix approach` and `## Test plan` from its `/sc:analyze` pass; "Not known yet" is not allowed in these three sections; where the pass leaves a gap, the worker states its assumption in the section and lists it in `draft-notes.md`; every other section keeps the "Not known yet" rule.
66	
67	- **Priority**: exactly one of Urgent, High, Medium or Low, then a one-line reason that names the trigger of the rule it follows from the rule set below. Never blank.
68	- **Fix approach**: the ordered steps to do the work; for each step the files or components it touches (taken from the `/sc:analyze` pass); the SC commands or skills to run in order (for example `/sc:workflow`, then `/sc:implement`, then `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3`); and the repo and the base branch.
69	- **Test plan**: the tests to add or change, the regression gate (the full suite, lint and sync checks), and how a reviewer verifies the result.
70	
71	An assumption the worker makes where the pass leaves a gap goes under "New material" in `draft-notes.md`, one line per assumption, starting with "Assumption:". Assumptions are kept and never cause a question.
72	
73	The Priority rule set is defined once, here; the templates and the workers point at it.
74	
75	| Level | Trigger |
76	|---|---|
77	| Urgent | Data loss, a security exposure, or a broken release or gate with no workaround. |
78	| High | A documented command or gate fails, or other work is blocked. |
79	| Medium | Degraded behaviour with a workaround, or a planned feature. |
80	| Low | Cosmetic, wording, or docs only. |
81	
82	Choose the highest level whose trigger the issue meets.
83	
84	### Contradiction prompt rule (default D14)
85	
86	Ask only when `draft-notes.md` lists a supported contradiction of the user's own description, instruction or flag: reversed choice, dropped requirement, changed flag, or a user-stated fact contradicted by verified code (each with the user's own words and the conflicting evidence). Empty notes, or notes with only `None` under both headings, ask zero questions and Wave 5 posts. One or more supported contradiction items ask exactly one question (AskUserQuestion), once per run, naming every item, with the choices "keep my wording" (change the draft to honor the user's words), "keep the draft" (accept the draft's change) and "edit". Apply the answer to `<D>/issue-body.md` before Wave 5; it changes only the contradicted items. Every New material item, assumptions included, stays in the body and in `draft-notes.md` whatever the answer, and is listed in the final output. A worker's disagreement with a supplied flag is not a contradiction when the issue is filed with the user's flag (Wave 2, line "The issue is filed with the user's flags when the user gave them"); it stays the pushback comment of Wave 5 step 7. The full body is never shown for approval (B1).
87	
88	## Wave 5: post (orchestrator, directly)
89	
90	Load `refs/labels.md`.
91	
92	1. Labels = the mode label only (`enhancement` for feature, `bug` for bug), intersected with the repo labels in `scout.md`. A missing one is listed in the final output, never created (B7). No label for the area or for the complexity is requested.
93	2. Issue type: the wanted type follows the rule of `refs/labels.md`. When it is listed under `### Repo issue types` in `scout.md`, the create command of step 3 gets `--type "<name>"`; otherwise omit the flag and remember `not set: issue type <name>: type missing in repo` (or `lookup failed`).
94	3. `gh issue create --repo <R> --title "<prefix><title>" --body-file <D>/issue-body.md --label "<label>"` (give `--label` only when step 1 kept the label; omit it when the repo lacks the label; plus `--type "<name>"` when step 2 allows it), with the prefix `[FEATURE] ` or `[BUG] ` (default D21). Failure -> STOP `E-CREATE-FAILED`; the draft directory is kept.
95	4. Read `<N>` from the issue URL that step 3 prints, then rename `<D>` to `.dev/issues/<N>/`.
96	5. Type read-back: `gh issue view <N> --repo <R> --json issueType --jq .issueType.name`. When `--type` was passed and the result is empty or different, remember `not set: issue type <name>: not applied after create`.
97	6. Complexity field: when `### Complexity field` in `scout.md` lists the field and an option equal to the wanted value (`quick` = Simple, `standard` = Medium, `deep` = Complex), write `.dev/issues/<N>/complexity-field.json` and run `gh api -X POST repos/<R>/issues/<N>/issue-field-values --input .dev/issues/<N>/complexity-field.json` (body and error handling in `refs/labels.md`). A failed POST remembers `not set: field Complexity <value>: write failed (<first line of the gh error>)`. After a success, read the values back with `gh api repos/<R>/issues/<N>/issue-field-values` and remember `not set: field Complexity <value>: not applied after create` when the value is absent. A missing field remembers `not set: field Complexity <value>: field not found in org` (or `lookup failed`).
98	7. Standard or deep with all flags given and a disagreement in Wave 2: write `.dev/issues/<N>/create-review.md` from `templates/create-review-comment.md` (it ends with `<!-- sc:issue:create-review -->`) and post it with `gh issue comment <N> --repo <R> --body-file .dev/issues/<N>/create-review.md`. Failure -> STOP `E-POST-FAILED`.
99	8. Print the issue URL, the directory, every `not applied: label missing in repo` line and every `not set` line (formats in `refs/labels.md`), one `kept without approval: <item>` line for every retained addition, and whether a contradiction question was asked and how it was answered. No ClickUp call (B6). No self-assignment. Do not stage or commit `.dev/issues/` (default D24).
100	
101	A failed type or field never stops the run once the issue exists. Only `gh issue create --repo <R>` (`E-CREATE-FAILED`) and the pushback comment (`E-POST-FAILED`) keep their STOP codes.

# /sc:analyze - Code Analysis and Quality Assessment

## Triggers

- Code quality assessment requests for projects or specific components
- Security vulnerability scanning and compliance validation needs
- Performance bottleneck identification and optimization planning
- Architecture review and technical debt assessment requirements

## Usage

```
/sc:analyze [target] [--focus quality|security|performance|architecture] [--depth quick|deep] [--format text|json|report]
/sc:analyze [target] [--output <file>] [--unattended] [--report-dir <dir>]
```

`--output <file>` writes the report to that file. A standalone run writes a file only when you pass it.

## Behavioral Flow

Before step 1, run the codegraph readiness check exactly once per run, as section 2 of `~/.claude/CODEGRAPH.md` describes: on the MCP path it first waits up to 60 s for a running `init` or `index` (guide step 3), and `checked_at` comes from one `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` Bash run right after the single `codegraph_status` call. Keep `index_state`, `access`, `checked_at` and `worktree_root` for the whole run and do not repeat the check. Below, "`index_state: fresh`" means `index_state: fresh` with `access: mcp` (the lookup tools are listed); with `access: cli` or `access: none` every step stays on Glob, Grep and Read, and no codegraph tool, including `codegraph_files`, is called.

1. **Discover**: Categorize source files using language detection and project analysis. When `index_state: fresh`, first call `codegraph_files {format:"grouped", maxDepth:2, path}` for the layout, with `path` set to the target's directory when the target is narrower than the repo; for a directory or package target add `codegraph_node {file, symbolsOnly:true}` on its main files, and use `codegraph_search` only when the target names a symbol
2. **Scan**: Apply domain-specific analysis techniques and pattern matching. When `index_state: fresh`, first call `codegraph_node` (symbol body with `includeCode:true` only for symbols Discover found, file outline with `symbolsOnly:true`), `codegraph_callers` and `codegraph_callees` for call paths (security: entry points to sinks; performance: hot-path callers)
3. **Evaluate**: Generate prioritized findings with severity ratings and impact assessment. When `index_state: fresh`, use `codegraph_impact` and `codegraph_callers` as dependency and blast-radius evidence for architecture and quality findings (dead-code candidates are leads only)
4. **Recommend**: Create actionable recommendations with implementation guidance
5. **Report**: Present comprehensive analysis with metrics and improvement roadmap, with one line `Codegraph: index_state=<state>, checked_at=<UTC>; degraded: <graph:* tokens or none>` (with `--format json` it is the top-level `"codegraph"` string field; a missing or stale graph leaves the run succeeded once the report is written)

Key behaviors:

- Multi-domain analysis combining static analysis and heuristic evaluation
- Intelligent file discovery and language-specific pattern recognition
- Severity-based prioritization of findings and recommendations
- Comprehensive reporting with metrics, trends, and actionable insights

## Tool Coordination

- **Glob**: File discovery and project structure analysis
- **Grep**: Pattern analysis and code search operations
- **Read**: Source code inspection and configuration analysis
- **Bash**: External analysis tool execution and validation
- **Write**: Report generation and metrics documentation
- **codegraph** (`mcp__codegraph__codegraph_status` once; then `_search`, `_node`, `_callers`, `_callees`, `_impact`, `_files`): used only when `index_state: fresh`, always before the matching Glob/Grep/Read step, which stays the floor

## Key Patterns

- **Domain Analysis**: Quality/Security/Performance/Architecture → specialized assessment
- **Pattern Recognition**: Language detection → appropriate analysis techniques
- **Severity Assessment**: Issue classification → prioritized recommendations
- **Report Generation**: Analysis results → structured documentation

## Codegraph (optional)

Full rules: `~/.claude/CODEGRAPH.md` (read it before the first codegraph call). This section is the short form for `/sc:analyze`.

- **Readiness**: the single check named before step 1 of the Behavioral Flow; never repeat it. `SUPERCLAUDE_CODEGRAPH_PRIMITIVES=off` means `graph:disabled`.
- **Use only when `index_state: fresh` and `access: mcp`.** Otherwise continue on Glob, Grep and Read, add the matching `graph:*` token to the report's Codegraph line, and go on: never halt, never ask. A missing, stale or failing graph never fails the run (it is succeeded once the report is written).
- **Leads, not citations**: re-Read a `file:line` before citing it (at `--depth quick`, a line found by Grep need not be re-Read, but a graph row cited as a finding is still confirmed by Grep or Read); an empty result is not a "no callers" finding; caller rows give the definition line, so confirm the call site (guide section 5) before citing; a caller list shorter than its total is `graph:truncated`; a single lookup that fails or returns nothing records `graph:empty` (or `graph:unresolved` for a row you could not confirm) on the Codegraph line and falls back to Glob, Grep and Read for that lookup.
- **Read-only**: never run `codegraph init`, `index`, `sync`, `explore` or `context`.
- **Names**: exact tool names `mcp__codegraph__codegraph_<tool>`, with `projectPath` set to `worktree_root` on every call.
- **Subagents** (if the run fans out): the brief carries `index_state`, `checked_at` and `worktree_root`; they call codegraph only when `index_state: fresh`.

## Examples

### Comprehensive Project Analysis

```
/sc:analyze
# Multi-domain analysis of entire project
# Generates comprehensive report with key findings and roadmap
```

### Focused Security Assessment

```
/sc:analyze src/auth --focus security --depth deep
# Deep security analysis of authentication components
# Vulnerability assessment with detailed remediation guidance
```

### Performance Optimization Analysis

```
/sc:analyze --focus performance --format report
# Performance bottleneck identification
# Generates HTML report with optimization recommendations
```

### Quick Quality Check

```
/sc:analyze src/components --focus quality --depth quick
# Rapid quality assessment of component directory
# Identifies code smells and maintainability issues
```

## Unattended mode

The shared rules are in `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`; read it first. This section lists only what `/sc:analyze` resolves itself.

- **Switch.** It applies only when `--unattended` is a standalone argument token outside any quoted argument; otherwise nothing here applies and no worker contract is written.
- **Report directory.** `--report-dir <dir>` only (`--output` is file-valued). Without it the run is refused before any work and the refusal is printed in chat only. A directory inside `.git/` or `.codegraph/`, one under the distributable skill, agent or command folders of a `.claude/` folder, or one that cannot be created or written, counts as no report directory known (refusal printed in chat only).

- Provide detailed reports with metrics and improvement guidance

**Will Not:**

- Execute dynamic analysis requiring code compilation or runtime

- Severity-rated findings
- Code quality metrics
- Security vulnerabilities
- Performance issues
- Recommendations

1	---
2	name: analyze
3	description: "Comprehensive code analysis across quality, security, performance, and architecture domains"
4	category: utility
5	complexity: basic
6	mcp-servers: [codegraph]
7	personas: []
8	---
9	
10	# /sc:analyze - Code Analysis and Quality Assessment
11	
12	## Triggers
13	
14	- Code quality assessment requests for projects or specific components
15	- Security vulnerability scanning and compliance validation needs
16	- Performance bottleneck identification and optimization planning
17	- Architecture review and technical debt assessment requirements
18	
19	## Usage
20	
21	```
22	/sc:analyze [target] [--focus quality|security|performance|architecture] [--depth quick|deep] [--format text|json|report]
23	/sc:analyze [target] [--output <file>] [--unattended] [--report-dir <dir>]
24	```
25	
26	`--output <file>` writes the report to that file. A standalone run writes a file only when you pass it.
27	
28	## Behavioral Flow
29	
30	Before step 1, run the codegraph readiness check exactly once per run, as section 2 of `~/.claude/CODEGRAPH.md` describes: on the MCP path it first waits up to 60 s for a running `init` or `index` (guide step 3), and `checked_at` comes from one `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` Bash run right after the single `codegraph_status` call. Keep `index_state`, `access`, `checked_at` and `worktree_root` for the whole run and do not repeat the check. Below, "`index_state: fresh`" means `index_state: fresh` with `access: mcp` (the lookup tools are listed); with `access: cli` or `access: none` every step stays on Glob, Grep and Read, and no codegraph tool, including `codegraph_files`, is called.
31	
32	1. **Discover**: Categorize source files using language detection and project analysis. When `index_state: fresh`, first call `codegraph_files {format:"grouped", maxDepth:2, path}` for the layout, with `path` set to the target's directory when the target is narrower than the repo; for a directory or package target add `codegraph_node {file, symbolsOnly:true}` on its main files, and use `codegraph_search` only when the target names a symbol
33	2. **Scan**: Apply domain-specific analysis techniques and pattern matching. When `index_state: fresh`, first call `codegraph_node` (symbol body with `includeCode:true` only for symbols Discover found, file outline with `symbolsOnly:true`), `codegraph_callers` and `codegraph_callees` for call paths (security: entry points to sinks; performance: hot-path callers)
34	3. **Evaluate**: Generate prioritized findings with severity ratings and impact assessment. When `index_state: fresh`, use `codegraph_impact` and `codegraph_callers` as dependency and blast-radius evidence for architecture and quality findings (dead-code candidates are leads only)
35	4. **Recommend**: Create actionable recommendations with implementation guidance
36	5. **Report**: Present comprehensive analysis with metrics and improvement roadmap, with one line `Codegraph: index_state=<state>, checked_at=<UTC>; degraded: <graph:* tokens or none>` (with `--format json` it is the top-level `"codegraph"` string field; a missing or stale graph leaves the run succeeded once the report is written)
37	
38	Key behaviors:
39	
40	- Multi-domain analysis combining static analysis and heuristic evaluation
41	- Intelligent file discovery and language-specific pattern recognition
42	- Severity-based prioritization of findings and recommendations
43	- Comprehensive reporting with metrics, trends, and actionable insights
44	
45	## Tool Coordination
46	
47	- **Glob**: File discovery and project structure analysis
48	- **Grep**: Pattern analysis and code search operations
49	- **Read**: Source code inspection and configuration analysis
50	- **Bash**: External analysis tool execution and validation
51	- **Write**: Report generation and metrics documentation
52	- **codegraph** (`mcp__codegraph__codegraph_status` once; then `_search`, `_node`, `_callers`, `_callees`, `_impact`, `_files`): used only when `index_state: fresh`, always before the matching Glob/Grep/Read step, which stays the floor
53	
54	## Key Patterns
55	
56	- **Domain Analysis**: Quality/Security/Performance/Architecture → specialized assessment
57	- **Pattern Recognition**: Language detection → appropriate analysis techniques
58	- **Severity Assessment**: Issue classification → prioritized recommendations
59	- **Report Generation**: Analysis results → structured documentation
60	
61	## Codegraph (optional)
62	
63	Full rules: `~/.claude/CODEGRAPH.md` (read it before the first codegraph call). This section is the short form for `/sc:analyze`.
64	
65	- **Readiness**: the single check named before step 1 of the Behavioral Flow; never repeat it. `SUPERCLAUDE_CODEGRAPH_PRIMITIVES=off` means `graph:disabled`.
66	- **Use only when `index_state: fresh` and `access: mcp`.** Otherwise continue on Glob, Grep and Read, add the matching `graph:*` token to the report's Codegraph line, and go on: never halt, never ask. A missing, stale or failing graph never fails the run (it is succeeded once the report is written).
67	- **Leads, not citations**: re-Read a `file:line` before citing it (at `--depth quick`, a line found by Grep need not be re-Read, but a graph row cited as a finding is still confirmed by Grep or Read); an empty result is not a "no callers" finding; caller rows give the definition line, so confirm the call site (guide section 5) before citing; a caller list shorter than its total is `graph:truncated`; a single lookup that fails or returns nothing records `graph:empty` (or `graph:unresolved` for a row you could not confirm) on the Codegraph line and falls back to Glob, Grep and Read for that lookup.
68	- **Read-only**: never run `codegraph init`, `index`, `sync`, `explore` or `context`.
69	- **Names**: exact tool names `mcp__codegraph__codegraph_<tool>`, with `projectPath` set to `worktree_root` on every call.
70	- **Subagents** (if the run fans out): the brief carries `index_state`, `checked_at` and `worktree_root`; they call codegraph only when `index_state: fresh`.
71	
72	## Examples
73	
74	### Comprehensive Project Analysis
75	
76	```
77	/sc:analyze
78	# Multi-domain analysis of entire project
79	# Generates comprehensive report with key findings and roadmap
80	```
81	
82	### Focused Security Assessment
83	
84	```
85	/sc:analyze src/auth --focus security --depth deep
86	# Deep security analysis of authentication components
87	# Vulnerability assessment with detailed remediation guidance
88	```
89	
90	### Performance Optimization Analysis
91	
92	```
93	/sc:analyze --focus performance --format report
94	# Performance bottleneck identification
95	# Generates HTML report with optimization recommendations
96	```
97	
98	### Quick Quality Check
99	
100	```
101	/sc:analyze src/components --focus quality --depth quick
102	# Rapid quality assessment of component directory
103	# Identifies code smells and maintainability issues
104	```
105	
106	## Unattended mode
107	
108	The shared rules are in `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`; read it first. This section lists only what `/sc:analyze` resolves itself.
109	
110	- **Switch.** It applies only when `--unattended` is a standalone argument token outside any quoted argument; otherwise nothing here applies and no worker contract is written.
111	- **Report directory.** `--report-dir <dir>` only (`--output` is file-valued). Without it the run is refused before any work and the refusal is printed in chat only. A directory inside `.git/` or `.codegraph/`, one under the distributable skill, agent or command folders of a `.claude/` folder, or one that cannot be created or written, counts as no report directory known (refusal printed in chat only).
112	- **Contract.** `<report-dir>/return-contract.yaml` is written on every outcome. `report_path` is the `--output` file, or `<report-dir>/analyze-report.md` when `--output` is absent. The run is succeeded when the report is written, and failed otherwise.
113	- **Gates.** There is no gate, and no person-mode flag. Under `--unattended` consent is never given: the rule "without explicit user consent" is not answered by assuming consent, so the command still modifies no source.
114	- **Nested invocations.** None.
115	- **Outward actions.** It pushes, commits and stages nothing.
116	
117	## Boundaries
118	
119	**Will:**
120	
121	- Perform comprehensive static code analysis across multiple domains
122	- Generate severity-rated findings with actionable recommendations
123	- Provide detailed reports with metrics and improvement guidance
124	
125	**Will Not:**
126	
127	- Execute dynamic analysis requiring code compilation or runtime
128	- Modify source code or apply fixes without explicit user consent
129	- Analyze external dependencies beyond import and usage patterns
130	
131	**Output**: Analysis report containing:
132	
133	- Severity-rated findings
134	- Code quality metrics
135	- Security vulnerabilities
136	- Performance issues
137	- Recommendations
138	
139	**Next Step**: After review, use `/sc:cleanup` for dead code removal.

@click.option(
    "--target",
    default="~/.claude/commands/sc",
    help="Installation directory (default: ~/.claude/commands/sc)",
)
@click.option(
    "--force",
    is_flag=True,
    help="Force reinstall framework files",
)
@click.option(
    "--list",
    "list_only",
    is_flag=True,
    help="List framework components without installing",
)
def install(target: str, force: bool, list_only: bool):
    """
    Install SuperClaude to Claude Code

    Installs the framework to ~/.claude/ and, as a required user-level phase,
    the pinned, checksum-verified codegraph binary registered as a user-scope
    MCP server (a failure there exits 1; --force is not forwarded to it). It then
    retires stale MCP registrations and the commands, skills and agents this release
    no longer ships, removing only what IronClaude can prove it installed.

    Examples:
        superclaude install
        superclaude install --force
        superclaude install --list
        superclaude install --target /custom/path
    """
    from .install_agents import (
        install_agents,
        list_available_agents,
        list_installed_agents,
    )
    from .install_ccsession import wire_ccsession
    from .install_commands import (
        install_commands,
        list_available_commands,
        list_installed_commands,
    )
    from .install_core import (
        install_core_files,
        list_core_files,
        list_installed_core_files,
    )
    from .install_hooks import install_hooks
    from .install_skill import list_available_skills
    from .install_skills import install_all_skills, list_installed_skills
    from .install_templates import (
        install_templates,
        list_available_templates,
        list_installed_templates,
    )
    from .install_user_setup import install_user_setup

    # List only mode
    if list_only:
        # Core files
        core_available = list_core_files()
        core_installed = list_installed_core_files()

        click.echo("📋 Core Framework Files:")
        for name in core_available:
            status = "✅ installed" if name in core_installed else "⬜ not installed"
            click.echo(f"   {name:35} {status}")

        click.echo(
            f"\nCore: {len(core_available)} available, {len(core_installed)} installed"
        )

        # Commands
        available = list_available_commands()
        installed = list_installed_commands()

        click.echo("\n📋 Slash Commands:")
        for cmd in available:
            status = "✅ installed" if cmd in installed else "⬜ not installed"
            click.echo(f"   /{cmd:20} {status}")

        click.echo(
            f"\nCommands: {len(available)} available, {len(installed)} installed"
        )

        # Agents
        agents_available = list_available_agents()
        agents_installed = list_installed_agents()

        click.echo("\n📋 Agents:")
        for name in agents_available:
            status = "✅ installed" if name in agents_installed else "⬜ not installed"
            click.echo(f"   {name:35} {status}")

        click.echo(
            f"\nAgents: {len(agents_available)} available, {len(agents_installed)} installed"
        )

        # Skills
        skills_available = list_available_skills()
        skills_installed = list_installed_skills()

        click.echo("\n📋 Skills:")
        for name in skills_available:
            status = "✅ installed" if name in skills_installed else "⬜ not installed"
            click.echo(f"   {name:35} {status}")

        click.echo(
            f"\nSkills: {len(skills_available)} available, {len(skills_installed)} installed"
        )

        # Templates
        templates_available = list_available_templates()
        templates_installed = list_installed_templates()

        click.echo("\n📋 Templates:")
        for name in templates_available:
            status = (
                "✅ installed" if name in templates_installed else "⬜ not installed"
            )
            click.echo(f"   {name:45} {status}")

        click.echo(
            f"\nTemplates: {len(templates_available)} available, {len(templates_installed)} installed"
        )

        click.echo()
        try:
            from .install_mcp import codegraph_list_lines

            for line in codegraph_list_lines():
                click.echo(line)
        except Exception as exc:
            click.echo(f"codegraph MCP: unavailable ({type(exc).__name__})")

        click.echo("\nRetired MCP registrations (user scope):")
        try:
            from .install_retired_mcp import list_lines

            for line in list_lines():
                click.echo(line)
        except Exception as exc:
            click.echo(f"   unavailable ({type(exc).__name__})")
        return

    # Step 1: Install core framework files to ~/.claude/
    click.echo("📦 Installing core framework files to ~/.claude/...")
    click.echo()

    core_success, core_message = install_core_files(force=force)
    click.echo(core_message)
    click.echo()

    # Step 2: Install slash commands
    target_path = Path(target).expanduser()

    click.echo(f"📦 Installing slash commands to {target_path}...")
    click.echo()

    cmd_success, cmd_message = install_commands(target_path=target_path, force=force)
    click.echo(cmd_message)
    click.echo()

    # Step 3: Install agents
    click.echo("📦 Installing agents to ~/.claude/agents/...")
    click.echo()

    agent_success, agent_message = install_agents(force=force)
    click.echo(agent_message)
    click.echo()

    # Step 4: Install skills
    click.echo("📦 Installing skills to ~/.claude/skills/...")
    click.echo()

    skill_success, skill_message = install_all_skills(force=force)
    click.echo(skill_message)
    click.echo()

    # Wire the installed ccsession skill before registering its hook.
    cc_success, cc_message = wire_ccsession()
    click.echo(cc_message)
    click.echo()

    # Step 5: Install hooks (scripts + additive settings.json merge)
    click.echo("📦 Installing hooks to ~/.claude/hooks/...")
    click.echo()

    hooks_success, hooks_message = install_hooks(force=force)
    click.echo(hooks_message)
    click.echo()

    # Step 6: Install document/workflow templates (PRD, TDD, MDTM, etc.)
    # Never writes into ~/.claude/agent-memory/ — that directory is owned
    # by per-agent runtime memory and is explicitly out of scope.
    click.echo("📦 Installing templates to ~/.claude/templates/...")
    click.echo()

    templates_success, templates_message = install_templates(force=force)
    click.echo(templates_message)
    click.echo()

    # Step 7: Shared user setup: rules (never auto-loaded), output styles,
    # settings defaults for keys the user has not set, and Orca's skills.
    click.echo("📦 Installing rules, output styles, settings defaults, Orca skills...")
    click.echo()

    setup_success, setup_message = install_user_setup(force=force)
    click.echo(setup_message)

    # Step 8: codegraph, a required user-level phase. A failure keeps the framework
    # work above, still runs the retire step below and exits 1. ``--force`` is not
    # forwarded: the phase is idempotent and only repairs what differs.
    click.echo("\n📦 Installing codegraph (required user-level phase)...")
    try:
        from .install_mcp import install_codegraph_mcp

        codegraph_success, codegraph_message = install_codegraph_mcp(scope="user")
    except Exception as exc:
        codegraph_success = False
        codegraph_message = (
            f"codegraph phase failed ({type(exc).__name__}); fix the cause and "
            "rerun superclaude install."
        )
    click.echo(codegraph_message, err=not codegraph_success)

    # Step 9: retire stale MCP registrations IronClaude can prove it wrote.
    # Non-fatal by design: nothing here may change the exit code.
    click.echo("\n📦 Retiring stale MCP registrations...")
    try:
        from .install_mcp import codegraph_ready
        from .install_retired_mcp import run_retire_step

        # A failed phase in this run never counts as ready (spec 2.12).
        run_retire_step(codegraph_success and codegraph_ready()[0])
    except Exception as exc:
        click.echo(
            f"   ⚠️  Retire step skipped ({type(exc).__name__}); install is complete."
        )

    # Step 10: retire commands, skills and agents this release no longer ships, but
    # only files whose content proves IronClaude installed them. Non-fatal by design.
    click.echo(
        "\n📦 Retiring commands, skills and agents this release no longer ships..."
    )
    try:
        from .install_retired_files import run_retire_files_step

        run_retire_files_step(target_path)
    except Exception as exc:
        click.echo(
            f"   ⚠️  Retire step skipped ({type(exc).__name__}); install is complete."
        )

    if (
        not core_success
        or not cmd_success
        or not agent_success
        or not skill_success
        or not cc_success
        or not hooks_success
        or not templates_success
        or not setup_success
        or not codegraph_success
    ):
        sys.exit(1)


@main.command()
@click.option(
    "--servers",
    "-s",
    multiple=True,
    help="Specific MCP servers to install (repeatable)",
)
@click.option(
    "--list", "list_only", is_flag=True, help="List available MCP servers (read-only)"
)
@click.option(

@click.option(

)

"""
Batch Skill Installation

Installs all SuperClaude skills to ~/.claude/skills/ directory.
Wraps the single-skill installer for batch operation during `superclaude install`.

Skills whose directory name starts with "sc-" and have a corresponding
slash command (e.g. a hypothetical bare "sc-foo" → commands/foo.md) are
served via /sc:<name> commands and are NOT installed as separate skills,
to avoid duplicate autocomplete entries. A command that explicitly activates
its matching skill is not self-contained, so that skill remains installed.

IMPORTANT (protocol-skill install policy): the project's protocol skills are
named "sc-<command>-protocol" (e.g. sc-reflect-protocol, backing commands/reflect.md).
These are INTENTIONALLY installed standalone, because each /sc:<command> command
activates its skill by name via `> Skill sc:<command>-protocol`; if they were
treated as command-backed and removed, that activation would break. The match
below therefore strips ONLY the "sc-" prefix and MUST NOT be generalized to also
strip a "-protocol" suffix — doing so would sweep every existing protocol skill
into the served-by-command removal path. See tests/unit/test_cli_install.py for
the regression guard that locks this behavior.

import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Tuple

from .install_skill import install_skill_command, list_available_skills

_SKILL_ACTIVATION_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*>?\s*Skill\s+([A-Za-z0-9:_-]+)\s*$", re.MULTILINE

    """Check if an sc-* skill is fully served by a matching slash command.

    For example, a bare skill "sc-foo" has a command if
    src/superclaude/commands/foo.md exists. A command that activates the skill
    by name is only an entry point, so the backing skill must remain installed.

    Note: this strips ONLY the "sc-" prefix. Protocol skills named
    "sc-<command>-protocol" therefore do NOT match commands/<command>.md and
    are correctly installed standalone (their /sc: command activates them by
    name). Do NOT add "-protocol" stripping here — see module docstring.
    """
    if not skill_name.startswith("sc-"):
        return False
    cmd_name = skill_name[3:]  # strip "sc-" prefix only (NOT a "-protocol" suffix)
    package_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    command_path = package_root / "commands" / f"{cmd_name}.md"
    return command_path.exists() and skill_name not in skill_activation_targets(
        command_path
    )


def install_all_skills(
    target_path: Path = None, force: bool = False
) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
    """
    Install all available SuperClaude skills to Claude Code

    Args:
        target_path: Target installation directory (default: ~/.claude/skills)
        force: Force reinstall if skills exist

    Returns:
        Tuple of (success: bool, message: str)
    """
    if target_path is None:
        target_path = Path.home() / ".claude" / "skills"

    available = list_available_skills()

    if not available:
        return True, "No skills available to install"

    installed = []
    skipped = []
    failed = []
    served_by_command = []

    for skill_name in available:
        # Skip sc-* skills that have a corresponding /sc: command
        if _has_corresponding_command(skill_name):
            served_by_command.append(skill_name)
            # Remove stale install if present
            stale = target_path / skill_name
            if stale.exists():
                import shutil

                shutil.rmtree(stale)
            continue

        skill_target = target_path / skill_name

        if skill_target.exists() and not force:
            skipped.append(skill_name)
            continue

        success, message = install_skill_command(
            skill_name=skill_name,
            target_path=target_path,
            force=force,
        )

        if success:
            installed.append(skill_name)
        else:
            failed.append(f"{skill_name}: {message}")

    messages = []

    if installed:
        messages.append(f"✅ Installed {len(installed)} skills:")
        for name in installed:
            messages.append(f"   - {name}")

    if served_by_command:
        messages.append(
            f"\n⏭️  {len(served_by_command)} skills served by /sc: commands (not installed as skills):"
        )
        for name in served_by_command:
            cmd_name = name[3:]  # strip "sc-" prefix
            messages.append(f"   - {name} → /sc:{cmd_name}")

    if skipped:
        messages.append(
            f"\n⚠️  Skipped {len(skipped)} existing skills (use --force to reinstall):"
        )
        for name in skipped:
            messages.append(f"   - {name}")

    if failed:
        messages.append(f"\n❌ Failed to install {len(failed)} skills:")
        for fail in failed:
            messages.append(f"   - {fail}")

    if not installed and not skipped and not served_by_command:
        return True, "No skills to install"

    messages.append(f"\n📁 Installation directory: {target_path}")

    success = len(failed) == 0
    return success, "\n".join(messages)


def list_installed_skills() -> List[str]:
    """
    List skills installed in ~/.claude/skills/

    Returns:
        List of installed skill names
    """
    skills_dir = Path.home() / ".claude" / "skills"

    if not skills_dir.exists():
        return []

    installed = []
    for item in skills_dir.iterdir():
        if not item.is_dir() or item.name.startswith("_"):
            continue
        # Check for SKILL.md or skill.md as indicator
        if any((item / m).exists() for m in ("SKILL.md", "skill.md")):
            installed.append(item.name)

    return sorted(installed)

2	Batch Skill Installation
3	
4	Installs all SuperClaude skills to ~/.claude/skills/ directory.
5	Wraps the single-skill installer for batch operation during `superclaude install`.
6	
7	Skills whose directory name starts with "sc-" and have a corresponding
8	slash command (e.g. a hypothetical bare "sc-foo" → commands/foo.md) are
9	served via /sc:<name> commands and are NOT installed as separate skills,
10	to avoid duplicate autocomplete entries. A command that explicitly activates
11	its matching skill is not self-contained, so that skill remains installed.
12	
13	IMPORTANT (protocol-skill install policy): the project's protocol skills are
14	named "sc-<command>-protocol" (e.g. sc-reflect-protocol, backing commands/reflect.md).
15	These are INTENTIONALLY installed standalone, because each /sc:<command> command
16	activates its skill by name via `> Skill sc:<command>-protocol`; if they were
17	treated as command-backed and removed, that activation would break. The match
18	below therefore strips ONLY the "sc-" prefix and MUST NOT be generalized to also
19	strip a "-protocol" suffix — doing so would sweep every existing protocol skill
20	into the served-by-command removal path. See tests/unit/test_cli_install.py for
21	the regression guard that locks this behavior.
22	"""
23	
24	import re
25	from pathlib import Path
26	from typing import List, Tuple
27	
28	from .install_skill import install_skill_command, list_available_skills
29	
30	_SKILL_ACTIVATION_RE = re.compile(
31	    r"^\s*>?\s*Skill\s+([A-Za-z0-9:_-]+)\s*$", re.MULTILINE
32	)
33	
34	
35	def skill_activation_targets(command_path: Path) -> set[str]:
36	    """Return the skills explicitly activated by a command file."""
37	    return set(_SKILL_ACTIVATION_RE.findall(command_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
38	
39	
40	def _has_corresponding_command(skill_name: str) -> bool:
41	    """Check if an sc-* skill is fully served by a matching slash command.
42	
43	    For example, a bare skill "sc-foo" has a command if
44	    src/superclaude/commands/foo.md exists. A command that activates the skill
45	    by name is only an entry point, so the backing skill must remain installed.
46	
47	    Note: this strips ONLY the "sc-" prefix. Protocol skills named
48	    "sc-<command>-protocol" therefore do NOT match commands/<command>.md and
49	    are correctly installed standalone (their /sc: command activates them by
50	    name). Do NOT add "-protocol" stripping here — see module docstring.
51	    """
52	    if not skill_name.startswith("sc-"):
53	        return False
54	    cmd_name = skill_name[3:]  # strip "sc-" prefix only (NOT a "-protocol" suffix)
55	    package_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
56	    command_path = package_root / "commands" / f"{cmd_name}.md"
57	    return command_path.exists() and skill_name not in skill_activation_targets(
58	        command_path
59	    )

62	def install_all_skills(
63	    target_path: Path = None, force: bool = False
64	) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
65	    """
66	    Install all available SuperClaude skills to Claude Code
67	
68	    Args:
69	        target_path: Target installation directory (default: ~/.claude/skills)
70	        force: Force reinstall if skills exist
71	
72	    Returns:
73	        Tuple of (success: bool, message: str)
74	    """
75	    if target_path is None:
76	        target_path = Path.home() / ".claude" / "skills"
77	
78	    available = list_available_skills()
79	
80	    if not available:
81	        return True, "No skills available to install"
82	
83	    installed = []
84	    skipped = []
85	    failed = []
86	    served_by_command = []
87	
88	    for skill_name in available:
89	        # Skip sc-* skills that have a corresponding /sc: command
90	        if _has_corresponding_command(skill_name):
91	            served_by_command.append(skill_name)
92	            # Remove stale install if present
93	            stale = target_path / skill_name
94	            if stale.exists():
95	                import shutil
96	
97	                shutil.rmtree(stale)
98	            continue
99	
100	        skill_target = target_path / skill_name
101	
102	        if skill_target.exists() and not force:
103	            skipped.append(skill_name)
104	            continue
105	
106	        success, message = install_skill_command(
107	            skill_name=skill_name,
108	            target_path=target_path,
109	            force=force,
110	        )
111	
112	        if success:
113	            installed.append(skill_name)
114	        else:
115	            failed.append(f"{skill_name}: {message}")
116	
117	    messages = []
118	
119	    if installed:
120	        messages.append(f"✅ Installed {len(installed)} skills:")
121	        for name in installed:
122	            messages.append(f"   - {name}")
123	
124	    if served_by_command:
125	        messages.append(
126	            f"\n⏭️  {len(served_by_command)} skills served by /sc: commands (not installed as skills):"
127	        )
128	        for name in served_by_command:
129	            cmd_name = name[3:]  # strip "sc-" prefix
130	            messages.append(f"   - {name} → /sc:{cmd_name}")
131	
132	    if skipped:
133	        messages.append(
134	            f"\n⚠️  Skipped {len(skipped)} existing skills (use --force to reinstall):"
135	        )
136	        for name in skipped:
137	            messages.append(f"   - {name}")
138	
139	    if failed:
140	        messages.append(f"\n❌ Failed to install {len(failed)} skills:")
141	        for fail in failed:
142	            messages.append(f"   - {fail}")
143	
144	    if not installed and not skipped and not served_by_command:
145	        return True, "No skills to install"
146	
147	    messages.append(f"\n📁 Installation directory: {target_path}")
148	
149	    success = len(failed) == 0
150	    return success, "\n".join(messages)
151	
152	
153	def list_installed_skills() -> List[str]:
154	    """
155	    List skills installed in ~/.claude/skills/
156	
157	    Returns:
158	        List of installed skill names
159	    """
160	    skills_dir = Path.home() / ".claude" / "skills"
161	
162	    if not skills_dir.exists():
163	        return []
164	
165	    installed = []
166	    for item in skills_dir.iterdir():
167	        if not item.is_dir() or item.name.startswith("_"):
168	            continue
169	        # Check for SKILL.md or skill.md as indicator
170	        if any((item / m).exists() for m in ("SKILL.md", "skill.md")):
171	            installed.append(item.name)
172	
173	    return sorted(installed)

@main.command()
@click.option(
    "--target",
    default="~/.claude/commands/sc",
    help="Installation directory (default: ~/.claude/commands/sc)",
)
def update(target: str):
    """
    Update SuperClaude to latest version

    Re-installs core framework files, slash commands, agents, skills, session
    setup, hooks, templates, and user setup to match the current package version,
    and removes the commands, skills and agents this release no longer ships when
    IronClaude can prove it installed them.

    Example:
        superclaude update
        superclaude update --target /custom/path
    """
    from .install_agents import install_agents
    from .install_ccsession import wire_ccsession
    from .install_commands import install_commands
    from .install_core import install_core_files
    from .install_hooks import install_hooks
    from .install_skills import install_all_skills
    from .install_templates import install_templates
    from .install_user_setup import install_user_setup

    click.echo(f"🔄 Updating SuperClaude to version {__version__}...")
    click.echo()

    # Update core framework files
    click.echo("📦 Updating core framework files...")
    core_success, core_message = install_core_files(force=True)
    click.echo(core_message)
    click.echo()

    # Update slash commands
    target_path = Path(target).expanduser()
    click.echo("📦 Updating slash commands...")
    cmd_success, cmd_message = install_commands(target_path=target_path, force=True)
    click.echo(cmd_message)
    click.echo()

    # Update agents
    click.echo("📦 Updating agents...")
    agent_success, agent_message = install_agents(force=True)
    click.echo(agent_message)
    click.echo()

    # Update skills
    click.echo("📦 Updating skills...")
    skill_success, skill_message = install_all_skills(force=True)
    click.echo(skill_message)
    click.echo()

    cc_success, cc_message = wire_ccsession()
    click.echo(cc_message)
    click.echo()

    # Update global hooks and their settings registrations.
    click.echo("📦 Updating hooks...")
    hook_success, hook_message = install_hooks(force=True)
    click.echo(hook_message)
    click.echo()

    click.echo("📦 Updating templates...")
    templates_success, templates_message = install_templates(force=True)
    click.echo(templates_message)
    click.echo()

    click.echo("📦 Updating rules, output styles, settings defaults, Orca skills...")
    setup_success, setup_message = install_user_setup(force=True)
    click.echo(setup_message)

    # Retire commands, skills and agents this release no longer ships (proven files
    # only). Non-fatal by design: nothing here may change the exit code.
    click.echo(
        "\n📦 Retiring commands, skills and agents this release no longer ships..."
    )
    try:
        from .install_retired_files import run_retire_files_step

        run_retire_files_step(target_path)
    except Exception as exc:
        click.echo(
            f"   ⚠️  Retire step skipped ({type(exc).__name__}); update is complete."
        )

    # Read-only: update never touches MCP registrations.
    try:
        from .install_retired_mcp import update_notice

        notice = update_notice()
        if notice:
            click.echo(f"\n{notice}")
    except Exception:
        pass

    if not all(
        (
            core_success,
            cmd_success,
            agent_success,
            skill_success,
            cc_success,
            hook_success,
            templates_success,
            setup_success,
        )
    ):
        sys.exit(1)


@main.command()
@click.argument("skill_name")
@click.option(
    "--target",
    default="~/.claude/skills",
    help="Installation directory (default: ~/.claude/skills)",
)
@click.option(
    "--force",
    is_flag=True,
    help="Force reinstall if skill already exists",
)
def install_skill(skill_name: str, target: str, force: bool):
    """
    Install a SuperClaude skill to Claude Code

    SKILL_NAME: Name of the skill to install (e.g., confidence-check)

    Example:
        superclaude install-skill confidence-check
        superclaude install-skill confidence-check --target ~/.claude/skills --force
    """
    from .install_skill import install_skill_command

    target_path = Path(target).expanduser()

    click.echo(f"📦 Installing skill '{skill_name}' to {target_path}...")

    success, message = install_skill_command(
        skill_name=skill_name, target_path=target_path, force=force
    )

"""Tests for the in-package ``superclaude update`` command."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest
from click.testing import CliRunner

from superclaude.cli.main import main

_INSTALLERS = (
    "superclaude.cli.install_core.install_core_files",
    "superclaude.cli.install_commands.install_commands",
    "superclaude.cli.install_agents.install_agents",
    "superclaude.cli.install_skills.install_all_skills",
    "superclaude.cli.install_ccsession.wire_ccsession",
    "superclaude.cli.install_hooks.install_hooks",
    "superclaude.cli.install_templates.install_templates",
    "superclaude.cli.install_user_setup.install_user_setup",
)

# Runs at the end of ``install`` only; ``update`` never touches MCP registrations.
_RETIRE_STEP = "superclaude.cli.install_retired_mcp.run_retire_step"
# Required phase of ``install`` only, between user setup and the retire step.
_CODEGRAPH_PHASE = "superclaude.cli.install_mcp.install_codegraph_mcp"


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def isolated_home_guard(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    from superclaude.cli import install_user_setup

    home = tmp_path / "isolated-home"
    home.mkdir()
    monkeypatch.setenv("HOME", str(home))
    monkeypatch.setenv("CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR", str(home / "config"))
    state = SimpleNamespace(home=home)
    # The existing real-framework ccsession fixture must not download plugins,
    # Orca skills or a browser while exercising the real install.
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        install_user_setup, "install_plugins", lambda **kwargs: (True, "Plugin fixture")
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        install_user_setup,
        "configure_playwright_browser",
        lambda **kwargs: (True, "Browser fixture"),
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        install_user_setup,
        "install_orca_skills",
        lambda **kwargs: (True, "Orca fixture"),
    )
    # The codegraph phase would download and register a real binary.
    monkeypatch.setattr(_CODEGRAPH_PHASE, lambda **kwargs: (True, "codegraph fixture"))
    return state


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _no_ccsession_permission_env(monkeypatch):
    """Keep the developer's shell out of the real ccsession run.

    ``test_real_install_launches_ccsession`` runs the installed ccsession with the
    inherited environment, and ccsession exits 2 on a bad CCSESSION_PERMISSIONS
    (and CC_CLAUDE_FLAGS would change its launch flags).
    """
    monkeypatch.delenv("CCSESSION_PERMISSIONS", raising=False)
    monkeypatch.delenv("CC_CLAUDE_FLAGS", raising=False)


def _stub_installers(monkeypatch, *, failing: str | None = None):
    calls: list[str] = []

    for path in _INSTALLERS:
        name = path.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]

        def fake(*args, _name=name, **kwargs):
            calls.append(_name)
            return (_name != failing, f"{_name} result")

        monkeypatch.setattr(path, fake)

    def codegraph(**kwargs):
        calls.append("install_codegraph_mcp")
        return (failing != "install_codegraph_mcp", "install_codegraph_mcp result")

    def retire(*args, **kwargs):
        calls.append("run_retire_step")
        return {}

    monkeypatch.setattr(_CODEGRAPH_PHASE, codegraph)
    monkeypatch.setattr(_RETIRE_STEP, retire)
    return calls


def test_update_refreshes_hooks_after_other_components(monkeypatch):
    calls = _stub_installers(monkeypatch)

    result = CliRunner().invoke(main, ["update"])

    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert calls == [
        "install_core_files",
        "install_commands",
        "install_agents",
        "install_all_skills",

        "install_hooks",
        "install_templates",

        capture_output=True,

@pytest.mark.parametrize("command", ["install", "update"])
def test_upgrade_from_an_installed_5_0_0(home, release_5_0_0, monkeypatch, command):
    _install_5_0_0(home, release_5_0_0)
    claude = _claude(home)
    commands = claude / "commands" / "sc"
    skills = claude / "skills"
    # a customized copy, a skill folder with an extra file, and unrelated user files
    custom = commands / "roadmap.md"
    custom.write_text(custom.read_text() + "\nmy own tweak\n")
    extra = skills / "sc-tasklist-protocol" / "my-notes.md"
    extra.write_text("my notes")
    user_command = commands / "my-own-command.md"
    user_command.write_text("mine")
    user_skill = skills / "my-own-skill" / "SKILL.md"
    user_skill.parent.mkdir()
    user_skill.write_text("mine")
    src = REPO / "src" / "superclaude"
    # items 6.0.0 still ships: present afterwards, equal to the shipped copy
    kept_6_0_0 = {
        commands / "implement.md": src / "commands" / "implement.md",
        skills / "sc-implement-protocol" / "SKILL.md": src
        / "skills"
        / "sc-implement-protocol"
        / "SKILL.md",
        claude / "agents" / "rf-qa.md": src / "agents" / "rf-qa.md",
    }
    _stub_risky_installers(monkeypatch)

    result = CliRunner().invoke(
        main, [command, *(["--force"] if command == "install" else [])]
    )

    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    expected_gone = [n for n in RETIRED_COMMANDS_5_0_0 if n != "roadmap"]
    assert not [n for n in expected_gone if (commands / f"{n}.md").exists()]
    assert not [
        n
        for n in RETIRED_SKILLS_5_0_0
        if n != "sc-tasklist-protocol" and (skills / n).exists()
    ]
    # kept and explained
    assert custom.exists() and "my own tweak" in custom.read_text()
    assert extra.exists() and (skills / "sc-tasklist-protocol" / "SKILL.md").exists()
    assert "Kept /sc:roadmap" in result.output and f"rm {custom}" in result.output
    assert "Kept skill sc-tasklist-protocol" in result.output
    assert "my-notes.md" in result.output
    assert f"rm -r {skills / 'sc-tasklist-protocol'}" in result.output
    # untouched
    assert user_command.read_text() == "mine" and user_skill.read_text() == "mine"
    for path, shipped in kept_6_0_0.items():
        assert path.read_bytes() == shipped.read_bytes(), path
    assert (commands / "sweep.md").exists()  # a 6.0.0 command is installed

    # a second run changes nothing and is not alarming
    before = _snapshot(claude)
    again = CliRunner().invoke(
        main, [command, *(["--force"] if command == "install" else [])]
    )
    assert again.exit_code == 0, again.output
    assert _snapshot(claude) == before
    assert "Removed" not in again.output.split("Retiring commands")[-1]
    assert "⚠️" not in again.output.split("Retiring commands")[-1]

def test_cli_integration():
    """
    Integration test: verify CLI can import and use install functions

    This tests that the CLI main.py can successfully import the functions
    """
    from superclaude.cli.install_commands import (
        list_available_commands,
    )

    # Should not raise ImportError

    assert len(commands) > 0


class TestProtocolSkillInstallMapping:
    """F2 regression guard (sc:reflect 2026-06-03): protocol skills stay standalone.

    The installer's ``_has_corresponding_command`` strips ONLY the ``sc-`` prefix.
    Protocol skills are named ``sc-<command>-protocol`` (e.g. sc-reflect-protocol
    backing commands/reflect.md) and are therefore NOT command-backed -- they are
    installed standalone, which is required because each /sc:<command> command
    activates its skill by name via ``Skill sc:<command>-protocol``.

    These tests would FAIL if a future change generalized the match to also strip
    a ``-protocol`` suffix (which would sweep every protocol skill into
    ``served_by_command`` and remove its standalone install).
    """

    def test_new_init_lite_protocol_is_not_command_backed(self):
        from superclaude.cli.install_skills import _has_corresponding_command

        assert _has_corresponding_command("sc-init-lite-protocol") is False

    def test_sample_existing_protocol_skills_not_command_backed(self):
        from superclaude.cli.install_skills import _has_corresponding_command

        for name in ("sc-reflect-protocol", "sc-task-protocol"):
            assert _has_corresponding_command(name) is False, name

    def test_bare_sc_command_mapping_still_works(self):
        """The strip-``sc-`` behavior is intact: a hypothetical bare sc-<cmd> maps."""
        from superclaude.cli.install_skills import _has_corresponding_command

        # commands/analyze.md exists, so a bare "sc-analyze" WOULD be command-backed.
        assert _has_corresponding_command("sc-analyze") is True
        # Non-sc- skills are never command-backed.
        assert _has_corresponding_command("some-other-skill") is False

    def test_command_activated_skill_is_not_command_backed(self):
        """A thin command cannot replace the skill it explicitly activates."""
        from superclaude.cli.install_skills import _has_corresponding_command

        assert _has_corresponding_command("sc-recommend") is False

    def test_install_all_skills_installs_command_activated_skill(self, tmp_path):
        """The global install payload includes /sc:recommend's backing skill."""

<!-- /sc:issue bug template (complex). Copy to <D>/issue-body.md and fill every placeholder in place. Keep every heading. Write "Not known yet" under a heading when the description and the codebase pass give nothing; never invent a fact. The exception is ## Priority, ## Fix approach and ## Test plan: fill them at every depth from the codebase pass, never write "Not known yet" there, and state any assumption in the section (rules in refs/create.md). -->

## Bug Summary

`superclaude install` never reports how many skills it copied: its last line is whatever the final retire step prints (or the codegraph/retire warning), and no line anywhere gives a skills total. The user asks that the command print, as its last line, how many skills it copied. [synthetic run marker: qev-deep-flag-preserved-190117]

## Environment (OS, version)

- OS: Not known yet (the reporter's OS is not given). Code read on Linux 6.8.0-149-generic.
- Version: Not known yet for the reporter. Code read at package version 6.1.0 (`pyproject.toml:7`), branch `qev-run`, commit `862384852`.

## Current Behavior

Running `superclaude install` echoes the output of `install_all_skills` in Step 4 (`src/superclaude/cli/main.py:202-208`) and then runs the remaining steps (ccsession wiring, hooks, templates, user setup, codegraph, retire steps). Nothing after Step 4 prints a skills total, and nothing prints a count as the last line:

- The skills block prints `✅ Installed N skills:` only when at least one skill was installed (`src/superclaude/cli/install_skills.py:119-122`); when none were, there is no count line at all, and the early returns print only `No skills available to install` (`install_skills.py:80-81`) or `No skills to install` (`install_skills.py:144-145`).
- The last output of a successful run is the Step 10 retire step (`main.py:271-283`, output from `run_retire_files_step`, for example `   No retired commands, skills or agents present.` at `src/superclaude/cli/install_retired_files.py:280`), or the retire-skipped warning at `main.py:281-283`.
- When any step fails, the command ends with `sys.exit(1)` at `main.py:285-296`, again with no count line.

## Expected Behavior

`superclaude install` prints, as its final line of output, how many skills it copied, on every path that reaches the end of the command:

- After the Step 10 retire step and any warning it prints (`main.py:271-283`).
- Also when the run ends in `sys.exit(1)` (`main.py:285-296`): the count line is printed before the exit.
- "Copied" means the installed bucket of `install_all_skills` (`install_skills.py:83`, appended at `:113`, reported at `:119`). Skills skipped because they already exist (without `--force`), skills served by `/sc:` commands and skills that failed are not counted.
- When nothing is installed (including the early returns at `install_skills.py:80-81` and `:144-145`), the line still prints `0`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a checkout, run `uv run superclaude install` (use a throwaway `HOME`, because the codegraph phase downloads a binary and registers an MCP server).
2. Look at the last line of the output: it is the Step 10 retire output, not a skills count.
3. Search the output for a skills total: only `✅ Installed N skills:` (first run) or `⚠️  Skipped N existing skills` (rerun without `--force`) appear, in the middle of the output, and never as the last line.

## Impact Assessment (Severity, Blast Radius)

- Severity: low. Output only; no file, exit code or installed content is wrong. (Assumption: the reporter has not stated a severity.)
- Blast Radius: the `install` command in `src/superclaude/cli/main.py` and the batch skill installer `src/superclaude/cli/install_skills.py`. `superclaude update` (`main.py:356-461`) shares `install_all_skills` (`main.py:402`) and must keep its current output unless the maintainer decides otherwise.

## Error Messages

```text
Not known yet (no error is reported: the command runs to the end and prints no skills count)
```

## Codebase Context (from `/sc:analyze`)

Pass: `/sc:analyze --depth deep` by following `~/.claude/commands/sc/analyze.md`, on Grep, Glob and Read (codegraph and auggie were not available to the worker).

- `src/superclaude/cli/main.py:46` `install(target, force, list_only)`. `--list` returns early at `:174` and prints per-category "available/installed" counts only (`:138-140` for skills); it never reaches the install steps.
- `main.py:202-208` Step 4: `skill_success, skill_message = install_all_skills(force=force)`, then `click.echo(skill_message)`. Only the `(bool, str)` pair is consumed.
- `main.py:241-255` Step 8 codegraph (a failure message goes to stderr, `:255`); `:257-269` Step 9 retire MCP; `:271-283` Step 10 retire files (non-fatal, prints a warning on exception); `:285-296` exit check ending in `sys.exit(1)`.
- `main.py:356-461` `update` also calls `install_all_skills(force=True)` at `:402` and has its own exit check at `:449-461`.
- `src/superclaude/cli/install_skills.py:62-64` `install_all_skills(target_path=None, force=False) -> Tuple[bool, str]`. Buckets: `installed`, `skipped`, `failed`, `served_by_command` (`:83-86`); served-by-command skills are never installed (and a stale install is removed, `:90-98`); existing skills without `--force` are skipped (`:102-104`); `installed.append` / `failed.append` at `:112-115`.
- `install_skills.py:144-145`: `if not installed and not skipped and not served_by_command: return True, "No skills to install"`. This branch also fires when every skill failed, so the failure text built at `:139-142` is dropped and success is reported as True (see draft-notes.md; out of scope here, but it decides what "0" means on that path).
- Callers that depend on the `(bool, str)` shape: `tests/unit/test_cli_doctor.py:78` (`skills_ok, _ = ...`), `tests/troubleshoot/test_diagnostic_worker_contract.py:419` (`ok, message = ...`), `tests/unit/test_cli_install.py:688,721,792,948`.
- Test stubs of `install_all_skills` return a 2-tuple and accept any kwargs: `tests/cli/test_update_command.py:16-25,74-96`, `tests/cli/test_install_retired_mcp.py:514-534`; real skills are installed in `tests/cli/test_install_retired_files.py:560-576` and `tests/cli/test_update_command.py:187-196`.
- Existing install-output tests check order and exit codes, not the final line or a skills total: `tests/cli/test_update_command.py:128-143,280-333`, `tests/cli/test_install_retired_mcp.py:552-560`, `tests/cli/test_install_retired_files.py:603-712`. A search of `tests/` finds no assertion on a skills total or on the last line of `install` output.

## Related Issues

None found: the scout lookup for `superclaude install skills count` returned no possible duplicates (`scout.md`).

## Frequency

Always: no code path of `install` prints a skills total, so every run is affected.

## User Impact

The user cannot read, from the end of the `install` output, how many skills were copied; they have to scroll back through the per-step output (which is only printed when at least one skill was installed) or run `superclaude install --list`.

## Business Impact

Not known yet

## Cascading Effects

Not known yet

## Logs and Stack Trace

```text
Not known yet
```

## Attempted Solutions

Not known yet

## Proposed Solution

Print one final line, `Skills copied: N` (wording is an assumption), from `install()` after the Step 10 retire step and before the exit check, so it comes last on the success path and on the `sys.exit(1)` path. Get `N` from the installed bucket of `install_all_skills` without changing its `(bool, str)` return: add an optional keyword out-parameter (for example `counts: dict[str, int] | None = None`) that `install_all_skills` fills on every return path, and have `install()` pass a dict and read `installed` with a default of 0 (so stubs that do not fill it print 0). Leave `update` and `install --list` unchanged. Details are in Fix approach.

## For Development Team (Root Cause Analysis)

- Root Cause Analysis: `install_all_skills` returns only `(success, message)` (`install_skills.py:62-64,149-150`); the installed count exists only as `len(installed)` inside the message text (`:119-120`) and is lost to the caller. `install()` echoes that message mid-run (`main.py:206-208`) and has no later statement that prints a total; the command's tail is the retire step (`main.py:271-283`) and the exit check (`main.py:285-296`).

## Priority

Medium: degraded behaviour with a workaround (trigger of the Medium level in the Priority rule set of `refs/create.md`): the count is not shown, but `superclaude install --list` (`main.py:138-140`) or the `- <name>` lines of the Step 4 output give the same information; nothing fails, loses data or blocks other work, so High and Urgent do not apply.

## Fix approach

Repo: IronbellyOrg/IronClaude. Base branch: `integration`.

Commands, in order: `/sc:workflow` (turn this plan into a task plan), then `/sc:implement` (steps 1 to 4 below), then `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3 --head <branch> --title "..." --body "..."` (opens the PR with `gh pr create --repo IronbellyOrg/IronClaude --base integration`, waits for the Augment and Codex reviews, fixes confirmed findings).

Steps, in order:

- Step 1: expose the installed count without breaking the `(bool, str)` contract. In `src/superclaude/cli/install_skills.py` add an optional keyword parameter to `install_all_skills` (for example `counts: dict[str, int] | None = None`) and fill `installed`, `skipped`, `failed` and `served_by_command` on every return path, including the early returns at `:80-81` (all zero) and `:144-145` (installed is 0 there by construction). Update the docstring (`:65-74`). Do not change the return type: `tests/unit/test_cli_doctor.py:78`, `tests/troubleshoot/test_diagnostic_worker_contract.py:419` and the test stubs rely on the 2-tuple.
- Step 2: print the final line in `src/superclaude/cli/main.py` `install()`: create the dict before Step 4 (`:202`), pass it as `counts=` at `:206`, and after the Step 10 try/except (`:283`) and before the exit check (`:285`) `click.echo(f"Skills copied: {counts.get('installed', 0)}")`. Because the echo comes before `sys.exit(1)` (`:296`), it is last on the failure path too. Do not touch `--list` (`:88-174`) or `update` (`:356-461`) unless the maintainer decides otherwise.
- Step 3: add and change the tests listed in the Test plan (`tests/cli/test_update_command.py`, `tests/unit/test_cli_install.py`).
- Step 4: if the install output is documented, add the new last line to `docs/getting-started/installation.md` (section "What's Installed", `:337`); otherwise skip.
- Step 5: run the regression gate from the Test plan, then open the PR. Before pushing: `git remote get-url origin` must print the IronbellyOrg/IronClaude URL, `git fetch origin && git log HEAD..origin/integration` and rebase onto `origin/integration` if it has commits the branch lacks. Run Python only through `uv run`. Edit only `src/` and `tests/`; never stage `.claude/` mirrors (no `git add .claude/...`, no `git add -f`; no primitive is edited here, so `make sync-dev` is not needed).

## Test plan

`superclaude install` never reports how many skills it copied: its last line is whatever the final retire step prints (or the codegraph/retire warning), and no line anywhere gives a skills total. ## Current Behavior

Running `superclaude install` echoes the output of `install_all_skills` in Step 4 (`src/superclaude/cli/main.py:202-208`) and then runs the remaining steps (ccsession wiring, hooks, templates, user setup, codegraph, retire steps). - The skills block prints `✅ Installed N skills:` only when at least one skill was installed (`src/superclaude/cli/install_skills.py:119-122`); when none were, there is no count line at all, and the early returns print only `No skills available to install` (`install_skills.py:80-81`) or `No skills to install` (`install_skills.py:144-145`).
- The last output of a successful run is the Step 10 retire step (`main.py:271-283`, output from `run_retire_files_step`, for example `   No retired commands, skills or agents present.` at `src/superclaude/cli/install_retired_files.py:280`), or the retire-skipped warning at `main.py:281-283`.
- When any step fails, the command ends with `sys.exit(1)` at `main.py:285-296`, again with no count line.

`superclaude install` prints, as its final line of output, how many skills it copied, on every path that reaches the end of the command:

- After the Step 10 retire step and any warning it prints (`main.py:271-283`).
- Also when the run ends in `sys.exit(1)` (`main.py:285-296`): the count line is printed before the exit.
- "Copied" means the installed bucket of `install_all_skills` (`install_skills.py:83`, appended at `:113`, reported at `:119`). Skills skipped because they already exist (without `--force`), skills served by `/sc:` commands and skills that failed are not counted.

## Bug Summary

`superclaude install` never reports how many skills it copied: its last line is whatever the final retire step prints (or the codegraph/retire warning), and no line anywhere gives a skills total. The user asks that the command print, as its last line, how many skills it copied. [synthetic run marker: qev-deep-flag-preserved-190117]

## Environment (OS, version)

- OS: Not known yet (the reporter's OS is not given). Code read on Linux 6.8.0-149-generic.
- Version: Not known yet for the reporter. Code read at package version 6.1.0 (`pyproject.toml:7`), branch `qev-run`, commit `862384852`.

## Current Behavior

Running `superclaude install` echoes the output of `install_all_skills` in Step 4 (`src/superclaude/cli/main.py:202-208`) and then runs the remaining steps (ccsession wiring, hooks, templates, user setup, codegraph, retire steps). Nothing after Step 4 prints a skills total, and nothing prints a count as the last line:

- The skills block prints `✅ Installed N skills:` only when at least one skill was installed (`src/superclaude/cli/install_skills.py:119-122`); when none were, there is no count line at all, and the early returns print only `No skills available to install` (`install_skills.py:80-81`) or `No skills to install` (`install_skills.py:144-145`).
- The last output of a successful run is the Step 10 retire step (`main.py:271-283`, output from `run_retire_files_step`, for example `   No retired commands, skills or agents present.` at `src/superclaude/cli/install_retired_files.py:280`), or the retire-skipped warning at `main.py:281-283`.
- When any step fails, the command ends with `sys.exit(1)` at `main.py:285-296`, again with no count line.

## Expected Behavior

`superclaude install` prints, as its final line of output, how many skills it copied, on every path that reaches the end of the command:

- After the Step 10 retire step and any warning it prints (`main.py:271-283`).
- Also when the run ends in `sys.exit(1)` (`main.py:285-296`): the count line is printed before the exit.
- "Copied" means the installed bucket of `install_all_skills` (`install_skills.py:83`, appended at `:113`, reported at `:119`). Skills skipped because they already exist (without `--force`), skills served by `/sc:` commands and skills that failed are not counted.
- When nothing is installed (including the early returns at `install_skills.py:80-81` and `:144-145`), the line still prints `0`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a checkout, run `uv run superclaude install` (use a throwaway `HOME`, because the codegraph phase downloads a binary and registers an MCP server).
2. Look at the last line of the output: it is the Step 10 retire output, not a skills count.
3. Search the output for a skills total: only `✅ Installed N skills:` (first run) or `⚠️  Skipped N existing skills` (rerun without `--force`) appear, in the middle of the output, and never as the last line.

## Impact Assessment (Severity, Blast Radius)

- Severity: low. Output only; no file, exit code or installed content is wrong. (Assumption: the reporter has not stated a severity.)
- Blast Radius: the `install` command in `src/superclaude/cli/main.py` and the batch skill installer `src/superclaude/cli/install_skills.py`. `superclaude update` (`main.py:356-461`) shares `install_all_skills` (`main.py:402`) and must keep its current output unless the maintainer decides otherwise.

Print one final line, `Skills copied: N` (wording is an assumption), from `install()` after the Step 10 retire step and before the exit check, so it comes last on the success path and on the `sys.exit(1)` path.
